title: Vaerion event envelope (v1)
description: Canonical envelope of the Vaerion event spine (ADR-0002). Every meaningful action is a versioned, attributed envelope on one ordered spine. This is the journal-read form: seq >= 1, allocated by the run's single journal writer (gapless, monotonic, per-run). Emission-path constraints are stricter than this schema: `type` must be registered in spec/events/registry.json before it can be emitted; at read time unknown types are forwarded untouched (forward-compat duty).

v.description: Envelope version. Additive-only evolution within v1 (ADR-0002).

type.description: Event type. Must be registered in spec/events/registry.json at emit time (no ambient events); unknown registered-later types are forwarded untouched by intermediaries at read time.

seq.description: Per-run sequence number. Gapless, monotonic, 1-based; allocated exclusively by the run's single journal writer. Call sites never choose seq (E1102).

ts.description: Event time, RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision.

trace_id.description: Trace identifier; groups all envelopes belonging to one causal trace.

span_id.description: Span identifier; identifies the producing step within the trace.

actor.description: Who caused this event. Never optional (constitution D-D): nothing happens without a who.

kind.description: Principal kind of the acting entity.

id.description: CRN or stable identifier of the acting principal.

cause.description: Why this event exists — the causal pointer (constitution D-D). Journaled decisions and gates are themselves causes.

kind.description: Cause kind: a causing envelope, a journaled decision, a gate, an external trigger, or the run origin.

ref.description: Sequence number of the causing envelope, decision id, gate id, or null for the run origin.

payload.description: Event-specific payload. Structurally an object; per-type payload schemas are carried by the event registry as they are published. Payloads must be canonically serializable (no floats; E1901) and redacted before journaling where privileged.
